tldr_label: TL;DR: Russia launches one of its largest attacks hours after Trump says Putin wants a deal, Wall Street's slide deepens, and Anthropic closes its debut up 17%

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Russia fired more than 100 missiles overnight, hitting Kyiv's bridges and energy sites, and two missiles and a drone came down in Poland. [[TAG:danger:mass strike]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell 2% for a sixth straight loss and the Dow closed below 50,000. Asian markets tumbled on Friday, with Taiwan and Korea down more than 5%. [[TAG:danger:rout]]

tldr_bullets.label: Anthropic
tldr_bullets.body: ANT opened at $111.50 and closed its first day at $97.17, up about 17% from the $83 IPO price. [[TAG:success:debut]]

tldr_bullets.label: Shenzhen
tldr_bullets.body: CBS and the Washington Post judged that the three-way summit achieved little beyond pledges on oil output and nuclear restraint. [[TAG:info:modest]]

tldr_bullets.label: Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: Kuwait and Bahrain fended off more Iranian aerial attacks. Trump said Iran may be exploring chemical and biological weapons; Tehran called the claim baseless. [[TAG:warning:unverified claim]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Barrage After the Call
sections.summary: Over 100 missiles hit Ukraine hours after Trump told Europe Putin wants a deal

paragraphs.heading: Kyiv Bridges
paragraphs.body: France 24 reported Zelensky's statement that Russia fired more than 100 missiles overnight in one of its largest attacks ever. The National reported strikes on three Kyiv bridges after Putin vowed revenge for the Crimean Bridge attack, while France 24 cited the mayor saying two were damaged. The Moscow Times and Business Standard reported three killed in Kyiv. Glavnoe reported that nuclear plants cut output and emergency outages hit seven regions. [[TAG:danger:energy grid]]

paragraphs.heading: Poland
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg and Euronews reported that Poland said two Russian missiles and a drone crashed on its soil. TVP World and United24 said one was a Kh-101 cruise missile. Saudi Gazette and Mezha reported no injuries. Polish officials called it one of the largest such incidents since the full-scale invasion began. [[TAG:warning:NATO border]]

paragraphs.heading: Trump's Message to Berlin
paragraphs.body: Axios and CNN reported that Trump, calling into the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin from Air Force One, said Putin is tired and wants a deal, according to people in the room. No on-record transcript has been released. Tusk was reported to have said the remarks were received very cautiously. Sunday Guardian reported that von der Leyen said peace depends on putting Ukraine in a position of strength, and IEU Monitoring said the coalition pledged continued support next year and legally binding guarantees after any ceasefire.

sections.title: Markets: The Slide Deepens
sections.summary: S&P 500 falls 2% for a sixth straight loss; Asia tumbles; Brent near $90

paragraphs.heading: Wall Street
paragraphs.body: ABC News reported that on Thursday the Dow fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%, to 49,097.06, and the Nasdaq composite fell 2.3% to 23,879.20. Reports put the S&P 500 down about 2% for a sixth straight decline, and Motley Fool reported that Alphabet fell as Anthropic's debut put a fresh value on Google's stake. All three indexes fell despite Anthropic's strong debut. [[TAG:danger:sixth loss]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia
paragraphs.body: Saxo reported that Asian stocks tumbled on Friday after Wall Street's sixth straight decline. KuCoin cited a 4.9% fall in the Nikkei 225. Saxo's figures showed Korea's Kospi and Taiwan's Taiex each down more than 5%, though figures varied by time of capture. [[TAG:danger:Asia selloff]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil
paragraphs.body: HDFC Sky reported Brent up 0.3% to $92.2 but on course for a third weekly decline as Hormuz shipments recover, while Dealplexus showed Brent near $89.5. The gap likely reflects different timestamps and contracts.

sections.title: Anthropic: Debut Day
sections.summary: ANT opens at $111.50, closes at $97.17, up about 17%; valuation estimates differ

paragraphs.heading: The Trade
paragraphs.body: Invezz reported that ANT opened at $111.50, touched $115 and closed at $97.17, up about 17% from the $83 IPO price, on volume above 846 million shares. Bloomberg, Forbes and Deadline also reported a roughly 17% first-day gain, with Deadline calling the session volatile. [[TAG:success:up 17%]]

paragraphs.heading: Valuation
paragraphs.body: Estimates conflict. Yahoo Finance and Forbes cited about $1.27 trillion, while CNN put the value at $1.76 trillion, apparently on a fully diluted basis. The gain came on a day when the main US indexes fell more than 2%.

sections.title: Shenzhen: The Verdict
sections.summary: Analysts say the three-way summit yielded little; Huang scandal shadows the trip

paragraphs.heading: Little Achieved
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Trump, Xi and Putin agreed to boost oil production and reaffirmed that there can be no winners in a nuclear war, but appeared to achieve little. The Washington Post described Xi and Putin sharing the stage with a weakened Trump. CNN's takeaways said the summit gave Putin the public relations win he sought. NBC News reported that Trump has left China. [[TAG:info:modest]]

paragraphs.heading: Nvidia Shadow
paragraphs.body: Forbes reported that Nvidia's board chair dismissed a push to reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned amid allegations that a Chinese woman he was involved with may be an intelligence asset. Al Jazeera noted that no charges have been reported. [[TAG:warning:allegations]]

sections.title: Gulf: Attacks and Accusations
sections.summary: Kuwait and Bahrain repel Iranian attacks; Trump alleges Iran weapons work

paragraphs.heading: Kuwait and Bahrain
paragraphs.body: Arab News reported that Kuwait and Bahrain fended off Iranian aerial attacks, and the Times of Israel reported that Saudi Arabia also came under attack. CBS News reported that Iran appeared to be targeting US radar sites in Bahrain. The Nation said the attacks escalate the fight over the Strait of Hormuz. [[TAG:danger:attacks]]

paragraphs.heading: Weapons Claim
paragraphs.body: CBS News and Yahoo reported that Trump said Iran may be exploring chemical and biological weapons. Al Jazeera and IBTimes said no public evidence has been presented, and Yahoo reported that Iran's Foreign Ministry compared the claim to the case made for the Iraq invasion. Yahoo also reported that Trump is considering strikes in the new year. [[TAG:warning:no evidence shown]]

sections.title: Israel: Gaza and Coalition
sections.summary: Gaza ground operation continues past truce line; Eisenkot eyes a vote without majority

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: Al-Monitor and the Japan Times reported that Israel launched a ground operation in central Gaza as dozens of people fled. Xinhua said Israel described it as an operation beyond the ceasefire line to remove a threat. New Straits Times reported the army moved into a Hamas-controlled area. [[TAG:danger:truce strained]]

paragraphs.heading: Coalition
paragraphs.body: Haaretz and the Times of Israel reported that Eisenkot plans to bring a government led by him to a Knesset vote before his mandate expires, even without a guaranteed majority. The Media Line said coalition talks remain deadlocked, and the Jerusalem Post reported that unity talks with Likud continue. [[TAG:warning:no majority yet]]

sections.title: COP31 and the Horn of Africa
sections.summary: COP31 draft drops fossil fuel phase-out on final day; Ethiopia-Eritrea war fears grow

paragraphs.heading: COP31
paragraphs.body: RTE and Globe TV reported that a revised COP31 draft removed references to phasing out fossil fuels. Climate Current reported that the talks may run into overtime over fossil fuels and climate finance, and WHIO, carrying an AP report, said they entered the final day with few commitments. Globe TV said France's minister called the omission a black mark. [[TAG:warning:fossil language cut]]

paragraphs.heading: Ethiopia and Eritrea
paragraphs.body: The Japan Times reported that clashes between Ethiopia and Eritrea threaten to escalate into full-scale war, with Badme the focal point. Arab News, citing Reuters sources, reported that both armies have massed forces along the border. Addis Standard reported overnight drone and artillery strikes around Badme. Eritrea has dismissed the buildup reports as propaganda. [[TAG:danger:war risk]]
